text: Convert the following EER model in to the relational model. Indicate the primary keys and the foreign keys of the resulted relations clearly.
Consider a relation R (A, B, C, D, E, F) with the following set of functional dependencies over R: F={A > BEF,B> E,C > D,AC > B}

subquestions.label: a)
subquestions.text: Find all the keys that follow from the given FDs using attribute closure, showing how you obtained them.

subquestions.label: b)
subquestions.text: Is R in 3NF? Give reasons for your conclusion.

subquestions.label: c)
subquestions.text: Is R in BCNF? Give reasons for your conclusion. If R is not in BCNF, convert it to a set of BCNF relations.

text: Consider the following relations in a database created for a university.

subquestions.label: a)
subquestions.text: Use SQL queries to answer following questions.

subquestions.label: i.
subquestions.text: Display the module codes and name of all modules followed by students in year 3 of SE specialization in academic year 2018.

subquestions.label: ii.
subquestions.text: Display the hall id and the floor number of halls which are vacant on Monday in Engineering Building.

subquestions.label: b)
subquestions.text: Create a view named ClassDetails that contains class id, module name, year the module is offered, specialization, type of class and the size of the class for each class. (size of the class is the number of students following the class).

subquestions.label: c)
subquestions.text: Create a function which named-getAvialability which takes class id and module code as inputs and returns the number of more students that could be added to the class based on class size and the capacity of the hall.

subquestions.label: d)
subquestions.text: Create a trigger to ensure that for a class, students are not allocated than the capacity of the hall allocated for the class. (Hint: Use the function created in c)).
